analysis.title: US Consumer Daily: Earnings Quick Takes (DKNG, MNST, WYNN, SG, MAT, TXRH, SVV, BLMN, REF)
key_insights: Morning color from Briggs Barton: Tech is bouncing (QQQ +1.5%) after Semis/SOX fell 12% in one of the worst days on record. The group screens oversold technically, which could set up a sharp snapback. Flows showed a large-cap defensive bias, with demand in WMT, COST, KO and KDP.

DKNG (-25% pre-market) missed Q3 EBITDA and cut FY26 guidance well below expectations. The FY27 EBITDA guide was also disappointing. The pace of Predictions Markets investment caught investors off guard, and after a series of guidance disappointments it is hard to underwrite FY27 with confidence.

DKNG Q3 adjusted EBITDA was -$317m vs JPMe -$83m and Street -$68m. FY26 EBITDA guidance was cut $575m to $225m from $800m. FY27 EBITDA was guided to $900m vs JPMe/Street about $1.1b. The $575m cut is -$475m of incremental Predictions investment and -$100m of lower Core (about $60m unfavorable sports outcomes, $40m iGaming promotions).

DKNG positives per JPM: Q3 included about $350m of prediction market investment vs about $100m in estimates. Ex-prediction markets, Core EBITDA was about $30m. October Predictions consumer volume was 3x July, and the 2026 cohort is described as run-rating $350m gross profit with breakeven in 20 months. Negatives: iGaming GGR +7% y/y, net revenue +2%, customer acquisition spend +76%, and share losses. JPMe puts FY26/FY27 prediction-market losses at about $1b combined.

MNST (-6% pre-market) beat on revenue: Q3 revenue $2.56b, +16.7% y/y and 2.7% above consensus, with International +28.1% and US +8.2%. Adjusted EPS of $0.30 was in line. Gross margin of 54.7% fell 108 bps y/y and missed JPMe 55.5% on mix, aluminum plus Midwest premium and freight. October gross sales were +10.7% ex-FX. US pricing rose November 1. JPM rates it Neutral with a $49 PT at about 37.5x NTM P/E.

WYNN Q3 adjusted EBITDAR of $464m was 4% below JPMe and 8% below consensus. Macau is 'not getting better', with Golden Week flat and volumes declining into October month-end. Las Vegas looks better for Q4 (Formula 1, convention calendar, 2027 group pacing). The Al Marjan project in the UAE is on track for a September 2027 opening. JPM reiterates Overweight and cuts the PT to $112 from $115.
SG (+1% pre-market) reported Q3 SSS of -6.4% vs Street -8.5%, with October inflecting to +5% on +4% transactions vs Street +3% for Q4. The stock is up more than 100% since August.

MAT (-6% pre-market): management cited broad-based POS deceleration from late September, reaching full speed in October. Implied Q4 sales growth is about -9% to flat. JPM stays Underweight with a new Dec-27 PT of $13 (about 7x EV/EBITDA). EPS estimates are $1.32/$1.16/$1.20 for 2026/27/28.
TXRH (-5% pre-market) missed slightly on comps (+4.3% vs Street +5.1%) and restaurant margin (-18 bps). Q4-to-date comps are tracking +1.5% vs Street +3.5%.

SVV beat on Q3 comps (+4.2% vs Street +3.6%) and adjusted EBITDA ($75.9m vs Street $73.1m), but the Q4 outlook implies adjusted EBITDA of $77.6m vs Street $79.4m, a sequential deceleration. JPM rates it Neutral with a $14 PT.

REF reported a Q3 beat and raise: revenue +19.1% vs consensus +16.7%, active customers +23.4%, FY26 revenue guidance raised to $610-612m, adjusted EBITDA margin guidance about 14.2%. JPM rates it Overweight, PT $21.
BLMN (-1% pre-market) beat on Q3 SSS but guided Q4 below expectations.

Ralph Lauren Q2 adjusted EPS of $4.64 beat consensus $4.27 on +9.6% constant-currency revenue growth. Asia comps were +24% and global DTC comps +10%. FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance was raised to +6-7% and operating margin expansion to +80-100 bps. JPM Overweight, PT $464.

Tapestry Q1 FY27 adjusted EPS of $1.82 was about 16% above consensus $1.57. Coach grew +16% constant currency, and China +41% constant currency. FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $8.25-8.35 from $7.80-7.90. JPM Overweight, PT $211.

Celsius Q3 revenue was $847M (+16.8% y/y) vs consensus $800M, and adjusted EPS was $0.41 vs $0.34. The stock opened +9.6% but closed -2.3% on a tougher Q4 outlook: $20-25M of shipment timing reverses, and Alani Nu pipeline-fill laps. Gross margin fell 468 bps y/y. JPM Overweight, PT $48.

Dutch Bros: JPM cut the PT to $50 from $60 on new-unit AUV and SSS pressure and competition from SBUX and 7 Brew. SSS guidance moved to 'at least 5%' from 5-6%, and adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to about $380m from $385-390m. Shares fell about 16% post-market.

PENN Q3 land-based EBITDAR of $502m beat JPMe $497m and Street $495m. Interactive loss of -$18m beat Street -$27m. FY26 land-based guidance was raised, and FCF yield is above 20%. JPM Overweight, PT $24.

Molson Coors cut 2026 guidance: constant-currency net sales -1% to -2%, underlying EPS -16% to -19%. Q3 gross margin of 35.3% fell 376 bps y/y and missed. The Midwest aluminum premium is expected to run about $130m above last year.

CAVA Q3 SSS were +3.1% with slightly positive traffic, and FY26 SSS guidance was raised to 6-7%. The stock corrected to $54 vs an unchanged $80 PT, which JPM calls an expectations issue rather than a results issue and a level to buy.
Genius Sports Q3 revenue was $270M (+62% y/y), with FY26 guidance up 1%. Shares fell 16% on expectations for a larger raise amid a Nasdaq decline of about 6%. JPM Overweight.
Kontoor Q3 adjusted EPS was $1.50 vs Street $1.32, and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $5.40. The implied Q4 EPS of about $1.78 is below Street $1.89. JPM Overweight, PT $105.
APLE Q3 adjusted EBITDAre was $140MM vs Street $130MM, and RevPAR grew +7.3%. FY26 guidance was raised by $23MM. JPM rates it Neutral.

BOBS Q3 comps of +3.8% beat the Street's +2.0%. Gross margin of 45.7% missed on diesel and freight, and full-year gross margin is now expected to fall 20-30 bps. JPM Overweight, PT raised to $25 from $22.
AAP Q3 SSS were -1.2% vs Street +0.1%, EPS of $0.79 beat consensus $0.75, and FY26 EPS guidance is $2.75-3.10. JPM Neutral, PT raised to $57 from $55.

sector_views.rationale: Mixed results: Las Vegas and regional gaming are solid, while Macau is weak and DKNG's prediction-market spending is weighing on online sports betting earnings.
Revenue momentum at MNST and CELH is offset by margin pressure from aluminum, Midwest premium, freight and mix.
Mixed prints: TXRH and BROS are softer, CAVA is described as a buy on weakness, and the consumer is called 'super challenged'.

earnings_insights: DKNG Q3 2026 reported adjusted EBITDA of -$317m vs JPMe -$83m and Street est -$68m. FY26 EBITDA guidance was lowered to $225m from $800m. FY27 EBITDA guidance is $900m vs JPMe/Street est about $1.1b. Q3 revenue was $1.33b vs JPMe/Street est $1.38b/$1.41b.

MNST Q3 2026 reported revenue was $2.56b (+16.7% y/y), 2.7% above consensus. Adjusted EPS was $0.30 vs consensus $0.30. Gross margin was 54.7% vs JPMe 55.5%. EBIT margin was 28.8% vs JPMe/consensus 28.9%/29.9%.

WYNN Q3 2026 reported adjusted EBITDAR was $464m, 4% below JPMe and 8% below consensus. Macau EBITDA was $255m and Las Vegas EBITDA was $159m, 10% below JPMe and 12% below Street on a reported basis. Hold-adjusted Las Vegas EBITDAR was $183m. Encore Boston Harbor EBITDAR was $50m.
SG Q3 2026 reported SSS were -6.4% vs Street est -8.5%. October SSS were +5% on +4% transactions. Street est for Q4 SSS is +3%.
MAT implied Q4 2026 sales growth is about -9% to flat. JPMe EPS is $1.32/$1.16/$1.20 for 2026/2027/2028.
TXRH Q3 2026 reported comps were +4.3% vs Street est +5.1%, and restaurant margin fell 18 bps. Q4-to-date comps are +1.5% vs Street est +3.5%.

SVV Q3 2026 reported adjusted EBITDA was $75.9m vs Street est $73.1m, with same-store sales +4.2% vs Street est +3.6%. Implied Q4 adjusted EBITDA is $77.6m vs Street est $79.4m. FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance is $270-275m, and JPMe is $274m.

REF Q3 2026 reported EBITDA was $23M vs Street est $21M, on revenue growth of +19.1% vs consensus est +16.7%. FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $610-612M from $602-606M, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to about 14.2%.
BLMN Q3 2026 same-store sales beat, and Q4 guidance came in below expectations (no figures given in the note).
RL Q2 FY27 reported adjusted EPS was $4.64 vs consensus est $4.27. JPMe FY27 EPS is $19.09 and FY28 EPS is $21.44.
TPR Q1 FY27 reported adjusted EPS was $1.82 vs consensus est $1.57. FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $8.25-8.35 and revenue to $8.5-8.6B.
CELH Q3 2026 reported revenue was $847M vs JPMe/consensus est $809M/$800M. Adjusted EPS was $0.41 vs JPMe/consensus est $0.35/$0.34. Adjusted EBITDA was $199M.
KTB Q3 2026 reported adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $1.50 vs Street est $1.32. Revenue was $685M vs Street est $693M. FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $5.40 vs prior $5.25-5.35.
GENI Q3 2026 reported revenue was $270M and adjusted EBITDA was $87M, +1% vs Street est.

PENN Q3 2026 reported land-based EBITDAR was $502m vs JPMe/Street est $497m/$495m. Interactive loss was -$18m vs JPMe/Street est -$25m/-$27m. The note also cites total adjusted EBITDAR of $452m, 2-3% above JPMe/Street.
TAP Q3 2026 reported adjusted EPS was $1.46 vs JPMe/consensus est $1.35/$1.45. Net sales fell 1.6%, and gross margin was 35.3% vs JPMe/consensus est 36.9%/37.3%.
CAVA Q3 2026 reported SSS were +3.1% vs JPMe est +2.0%. FY26 SSS guidance was raised to 6-7%.
BROS Q3 2026 SSS were in line. SSS guidance is now 'at least 5%' and adjusted EBITDA guidance about $380m. Implied Q4 adjusted EBITDA is about $86m vs prior JPMe/Street est about $97m.
BOBS Q3 2026 reported comps were +3.8% vs Street est +2.0%. Gross margin was 45.7% vs JPMe/Street est 46.8%/46.4%.
APLE Q3 2026 reported adjusted EBITDAre was $140MM vs JPMe/Street est $133MM/$130MM. AFFO per share was $0.50 vs JPMe/Street est $0.47/$0.46.
